## Purpose
Provides symmetric encryption/decryption for user-supplied GitHub PATs stored at rest by the handoff feature, using Fernet with a key derived from the app's `SECRET_KEY` via HKDF.

## Shape
- `_derive_fernet_key(secret_key, info)` — derives a 32-byte URL-safe base64 Fernet key from the app secret via HKDF-SHA256.
- `_get_pat_fernet()` — lazily initializes and caches a module-level `Fernet` instance keyed by the fixed `_PAT_HKDF_INFO` info string.
- `encrypt_pat(plaintext)` / `decrypt_pat(ciphertext)` — the public encrypt/decrypt entry points; `decrypt_pat` re-raises `InvalidToken` for the caller to treat as "credential lost, re-enter."

## Why this shape
The module docstring is explicit: a key derived from `SECRET_KEY` (not `SECRET_KEY` directly) means a leaked JWT-signing key doesn't also decrypt stored PATs and vice versa; the single derived key uses no per-tenant salt because the threat model (server-side at-rest encryption against DB-only compromise) gets nothing from salting beyond "if the master key leaks, everything is gone" — so the simpler, salt-free design was chosen deliberately.
